summary: Dependency-only change: the `security` catalog pin for `next` moves from 15.5.23 to 15.5.24 and the workspace override floor is raised from `next@<15.5.18 -> ~15.5.18` to `next@<15.5.24 -> ~15.5.24` (comment cites GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 / CVE-2026-75604). The lockfile is regenerated to match: next, @next/env and the eight @next/swc-* binaries move to 15.5.24, and the dependents @clerk/nextjs and evlog are re-keyed. In this repository `next` is only a devDependency of @cipherstash/nextjs (whose published peer range `^14 || ^15` is unchanged, and tsup externalises it) and an optional peer of evlog, a runtime dependency of @cipherstash/stack. The lockfile and overrides are not published, so customers' installed next version and the shipped dist output do not change. The realistic failure is a local/CI one: a patch-level behaviour or type change in next/server or next/headers breaking @cipherstash/nextjs typecheck or tests. Impact is low. CI wiring that would catch that exists (frozen-lockfile install, nextjs typecheck, turbo test) but no CI results were provided. A side note for reviewers: this bump does not fix the CVE for customers, who pick their own next version.

behaviour_changes.description: The workspace `security` catalog pins next to 15.5.24 (was 15.5.23); @cipherstash/nextjs consumes it as a devDependency via `catalog:security`. Lockfile resolves next@15.5.24 and its @next/env and @next/swc-* platform binaries with new integrity hashes.

The pnpm override is tightened from `next@<15.5.18 -> ~15.5.18` to `next@<15.5.24 -> ~15.5.24`. In the lockfile this also rewrites the recorded `next` peer range of @clerk/nextjs and evlog to `~15.5.24`. Overrides only apply to installs of this workspace; they are not part of any published package manifest.

No change to the published @cipherstash/nextjs contract: its peerDependency stays `next: ^14 || ^15`, and tsup (default externals) does not bundle next into dist. Published @cipherstash/stack lists evlog 1.11.0 unchanged; next remains evlog's optional peer that consumers resolve themselves.

failure_scenarios.title: Patch-level change in next 15.5.24 breaks @cipherstash/nextjs typecheck or tests
failure_scenarios.trigger: next 15.5.24 (a security patch release) changes types or runtime behaviour of NextResponse, NextRequest or cookies() used by packages/nextjs.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: packages/nextjs is compiled, typechecked and tested against the catalog-pinned next. Security fixes in middleware or request handling can tighten behaviour that the middleware helpers or their tests rely on.
failure_scenarios.consequence: CI fails for the nextjs package or, if tests are not run, a local dev/test mismatch. Published dist is unaffected because next is external and the peer range is unchanged; customers run whichever next they install.

evidence.claim: Lockfile resolves next@15.5.24 (previously 15.5.23) with a new integrity hash; @next/env, @next/swc-*, @clerk/nextjs and evlog snapshots re-keyed accordingly.
Override `'next@<15.5.24': '~15.5.24'` with comment citing GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 / CVE-2026-75604.
@cipherstash/nextjs has next as a devDependency (catalog:security) and an unchanged peerDependency `^14 || ^15`.
tsup config does not set noExternal; by tsup's defaults peer dependencies such as next are external, so next is not bundled into dist.
@cipherstash/stack depends on evlog 1.11.0, whose optional next peer is resolved in the lockfile.
@cipherstash/nextjs imports cookies from next/headers and NextRequest/NextResponse from next/server.
The nextjs test suite imports NextRequest/NextResponse from next/server, so it runs against the installed next.
CI installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and later runs `pnpm run test` (line 357), which is `turbo test --filter './packages/**'` per the root package.json.
CI runs `pnpm exec turbo run typecheck --filter @cipherstash/nextjs`.
pnpm-lock.yaml is a frequent-change hotspot (246 commits, 83 in last 90 days); routine dependency churn, not itself a risk signal.
